title: The Open Day Competition
transcript:
Speaker 2: Claire: Hi, Grant. What sort of competition do you think we should organize?
Speaker 3: Grant: Well, Claire, the open day committee was pretty clear on that. It must be something with youth appeal.
Speaker 2: Claire: That makes sense. After all, most of the visitors will have just left high school.
Speaker 3: Grant: Yeah. So I was thinking technology.
Speaker 2: Claire: Do you mean something which uses the latest technology, like an iPod?
Speaker 3: Grant: Something like that, but a bit more expensive maybe.
Speaker 2: Claire: What about the latest iPhone? I’m saving up for one right now.
Speaker 3: Grant: Let’s make it an iPad. I wish I’d had a tablet computer when I started university.
Speaker 2: Claire: Yeah. That’s a great idea. That should get a lot of our younger visitors interested.
Speaker 3: Grant: Right. Let’s go with that then.
Speaker 2: Claire: Fine. We could go into town now and buy it. I saw great deals advertised at the Rick Smith store.
Speaker 3: Grant: Oh, I don’t think we’ll have to worry about that. A university purchase order will probably be arranged through the resources and supplies section.
Speaker 2: Claire: Well, that’s settled then. What about the competition? Is it going to be a game of skill or a guessing game or something else?
Speaker 3: Grant: What do you think would work best?
Speaker 2: Claire: Good question. I don’t think it should be anything too hard or anything that will make the visitors look silly. Some of them have such fragile egos.
Speaker 3: Grant: True. So something that anyone can do. Nothing competitive, no skill or intelligence involved.
Speaker 2: Claire: That’s right. But the main thing is that the contestants have a lot of fun.
Speaker 3: Grant: How do we do that?
Speaker 2: Claire: Well, I was thinking of a popular TV series, Science fiction or science fantasy. I don’t actually know the difference.
Speaker 3: Grant: Go on.
Speaker 2: Claire: It’s a series where in every episode, the main characters step through a portal into another world or another era.
Speaker 3: Grant: What’s a portal?
Speaker 2: Claire: It’s like a gateway or entrance to something.
Speaker 3: Grant: Okay. I get it. They’ll be stepping into the new world of tertiary learning. So somehow, we encourage people to step through this portal. Then what?
Speaker 2: Claire: They get their photo taken.
Speaker 3: Grant: Is that all?
Speaker 2: Claire: Not exactly. Let me think.
Speaker 3: Grant: I can’t see how that’s a competition unless we pick the best photograph. But there’s not much excitement or involvement in that for the participants.
Speaker 2: Claire: Wait. We don’t decide on the winner. I mean, no one person does. We get them, the public, to do it. How? Put all the photos on Facebook and the one with the most votes wins.
Speaker 3: Grant: I agree. Good idea. But there’s just one more thing I’m not clear about. How do we get hold of a portal?
Speaker 2: Claire: I was thinking graduates of the engineering department could construct it as part of their contribution to open day.
Speaker 3: Grant: How do visitors enter the competition on open day?
Speaker 2: Claire: Well, firstly, they have to make their way to the portal photo booth on campus.
Speaker 3: Grant: Okay. A bit like a treasure hunt to start with.
Speaker 2: Claire: Yes. And then they get their photo taken stepping through the portal.
Speaker 3: Grant: And they’ll have to write down their details. You know, name, phone number, email. No. Hang on. Let’s keep it simple. Just name and email address should do.
Speaker 2: Claire: Then after say the July 30, people can visit the university Facebook page and vote for their favorite photo.
Speaker 3: Grant: So the photo with the most votes wins.
Speaker 2: Claire: Yes. I think that should generate quite a bit of interest.
Speaker 3: Grant: What about a cutoff date?
Speaker 2: Claire: Of course. Maybe, the most popular photo as of 5PM on the August 10 will collect the iPad.
Speaker 3: Grant: And the winner will be notified by email.
Speaker 2: Claire: And the winning photo will be enlarged and published in full color on the university Facebook page.
